summary_en: LSMS-Net treats photoacoustic reconstruction in acoustically heterogeneous porous media as a recursive inverse multiple-scattering problem. Its layer-stripping pipeline progressively estimates and removes propagation effects, while a Ghost Network models non-local reverberation, an adaptive scattering point-spread-function layer captures wavefront distortion, and a spectral-consistency constraint compensates frequency-dependent attenuation. Simulation and phantom results show improved recovery of deep porous structures, making this a direct core contribution to computational photoacoustic imaging.
